title: SPA/258/2023 of KULDEEP KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
SRI JUSTICE VIPIN SANGHI, C.J.
AND
SRI JUSTICE RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
Special Appeal No. 258 of 2023
Between:
Kuldeep Kumar
and others. .......Appellants.
And
State of Uttarakhand
and others. .......Respondents.
Counsel for the appellants: Mr. A.S.Rawat, Sr. Advocate with Mr.
Gir Veer Chand, Advocate.
Counsel for the respondents: Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Deputy Advocate
General for the State.
Mr. C.K. Sharma and Mr. Harsh
Vardhan Dhanik, Advocates for
respondent no. 4.

Upon hearing the learned Counsel for the parties, the Court made the
following JUDGMENT : (per Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
1. Present special appeal is preferred by the appellants against
the judgment and order dated 06.07.2023 passed by the learned
Single Judge in Writ Petition (SS) No. 650 of 2023 (Kuldeep
Kumar and others Vs. State of Uttarakhand and others), whereby
the learned Single Judge dismissed the writ petition and upheld
the decision of Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection
Commission of cancelling the examination in respect of various
posts under Group C, which was initiated pursuant to
Advertisement No. 29/USSC/2020 dated 06.11.2020.
2. Various grounds have been taken by the petitioners -
appellants challenging the impugned judgment. In the present
appeal, one of the grounds, which has been taken by the
petitioners - appellants is that learned Single Judge overlooked

2
this fact that petitioners - appellants were some amongst the
large number of candidates, who have not indulged in any kind
of unfair means, and were selected purely on the basis of their
hard work, which they have been putting for the last many years.
3. Another ground is that there were a few persons, who were
indulged in making money by leaking the question paper, and,
they selected a few candidates, who in lieu of providing question
paper, paid some money to them.
4. Another ground for assailing the judgment of learned
Single Judge is that as per modus operandi of the accused, who
was a single person initially, he was posted at the printing site,
and he somehow obtained a copy of question paper on whatsapp
and sent the same to another person at Dehradun and, thereafter,
deleted the whatsapp content, and the individual at Dehradun
got a hard copy made from whatsapp and thereafter, deleted the
same from his mobile and, lastly, the hard copy was given to a
few agents in the field, and the agents approached some selected
persons of their own after having taken money from them, and
just 15 to 20 minutes before the examination, the paper was
leaked by way of a method of memorization and agents had
ensured that the copy with them does not in any way, go outside
of the room in which the candidates who paid the money, can
memorise the questions.
5. Mr. A.S. Rawat, learned Sr. Advocate for the petitioners -
appellants submits that question paper so leaked was confined
only to a few selected ones, and that too for a particular shift of
the examination, and the tainted persons have already been
identified and segregation was the only method of doing
complete justice. In order to substantiate his argument, Senior
Counsel for the petitioners - appellants further submits that the

3
Commission, as well as the State Government, has handed over
the investigation to a Special Task Force (STF) and the said
Investigating Agency had already identified the tainted
candidates and, therefore, present one is a fit case for segregation.
6. Learned Sr. Counsel for the petitioners - appellants in order
to substantiate the ground (G) of the appeal submits that the
Special Task Force has identified 115 tainted candidates and 42
agents and Hon'ble the Chief Minister has awarded them for this
job and despite this, learned Single Judge does not find it to be a
fit case for segregation and denied justice to the honest,
hardworking and untainted persons like petitioners - appellants.
7. First of all, a reference is being made to the reliefs, as sought
in the writ petition, before the learned Single Judge:
"i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of the
Certiorari quashing the office memorandum dated
30.12.2022 (Annexure No. 8 to the writ petition) issued by
respondent no. 4.
ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of the
Certiorari quashing the letter dated 10.04.2023 (Annexure
No. 9 to the writ petition) purposing to hold re-examination after cancelling the earlier one issued by
respondent no. 4.
iii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of the
mandamus directing the respondent authorities to
segregate the candidates who have been found to be
involved in malpractices or irregularities from that of the
persons those who are not tainted at all and issue an
appointment letter to them as a consequence of their final
selection in the competitive examination."

4
8. As it appears from the relief no. 1, petitioners - appellants
have challenged the office memorandum dated 30.12.2022 issued
by the Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection Commission
(recruiting agency). By this order, a decision was taken by the
Commission in its meeting dated 27.12.2022 for cancelling the
entire selection by recording the reasons that, though such a
decision will cause hardship to the innocent candidates, who
were not indulged in any unfair or malpractice, but to maintain
the purity of the examination this is the only option. At this
juncture, it is necessary to reproduce the said office memo. dated
30.12.2022 as under:

Recruitment to public services must command public confidence.
Persons who are recruited are intended to fulfil public functions

9. As it appears from the aforesaid office memorandum,
while taking the decision in its meeting dated 27.12.2022, the
Commission had also taken into consideration the judgments of
the Supreme Court. The most relevant aspect, as is reflected in the
office memorandum, is that while cancelling the selection, the
Commission has also taken a decision that only those candidates,
who participated earlier, would be permitted to appear in the re-examination, which was re-scheduled in the second week of
March, 2023.
10. By relief no. 2, letter dated 10.04.2023 was also challenged,
which is only a consequential order of the Commission, after
cancelling the examination by the office memorandum dated
30.12.2022, and by this letter only schedule of the re-examination
was published.
11. The main contention of the petitioners - appellants before
the writ Court was that petitioners are from very weak economic

7
background, and their family with very hard work have been
able to provide them higher education with an aspiration that
their ward would get a good job in his life, and would lead a
reasonable life ahead. It is further contended that the petitioners
have been preparing for competitive examination for the last so
many years and pursuant to the advertisement no.
29/USSC/2020 dated 06.11.2020, petitioners - appellants applied
for various posts in Group C. By this advertisement, a total 854
posts were advertised. It is further contended that petitioners-appellants were having all the essential qualification as required
for the posts so advertised. They applied for the posts pursuant to
the advertisement since they are Graduate and are eligible under
the advertisement. Thereafter, petitioners appeared in the written
examination, which was held on 04.12.2021 and 05.12.2021, in a
fair manner, and did not indulge in any malpractice and unfair
activities. After holding written examination, the Commission
notified the result of the combined examination on 07.04.2022,
with a clear direction that the date and place of document
verification and typing test would be published on Commission's
website. It is further contended by the petitioners-appellants, that
the Commission also made it clear that if any candidate has any
objection to the examination result, then he may file the same
within a period of 15 days from the date of declaration of the
result, and any objection received after 15 days would not be
considered. It is submitted by the petitioners-appellants that they
were selected, and they found a place in the select list. It was
further contended before the writ Court that the Commission,
vide its notification dated 29.04.2022, invited all the selected
candidates-including the petitioners-appellants for verification of
the documents and typing test, for which date was fixed from
17.05.2022 to 27.05.2022. Petitioners-appellants appeared before

8
the Commission and got their documents verified. After
completion of the document verification, the selection process
was practically concluded by the Commission. Despite this, no
appointment orders were issued to the selected candidates-including the petitioners-appellants for a long period and,
thereafter, when selected candidates enquired why appointment
letters were not issued despite their selection and after due
verification of the documents, then, the Commission informed
that some complaints regarding use of unfair means and
irregularity about the examination are received, and the
Commission informed them that they are trying to find out the
truth of the complaints, and assured that petitioners-appellants
and other persons, who did not indulge in unfair practice, that
they would be segregated, and their appointment would be done
shortly. It is further contended by the petitioners-appellants in
the writ petition, that Commission lodged an FIR on 22.07.2022
and the investigation was handed over to Special Task Force. The
Special Task Force held the preliminary inquiry. Since no
appointment letters were issued by the Commission despite the
fact that the Special Task Force identified the tainted persons,
some of the applicants filed Writ Petition (SS) No. 1304 of 2022
before this Court, and this Court vide order dated 18.07.2022
directed the Authorities to complete the inquiry within ten
weeks. The relevant extract of the order dated 18.07.2022 passed
by this Court reads as under:
"That Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection Commission
issued an advertisement on 06.11.2020, inviting applications
from eligible candidates for appointment to different Group 'C'
posts under various Government Departments. Petitioners
responded to the said advertisement and they were permitted
to appear in the written examination, which was held on 4th
& 5th December, 2021. Result of the said examination was

9
published on 07.04.2022 and, thereafter, document verification
was done by the Selecting Body on 19.05.2022. It is not in
dispute that petitioners were called for document verification
and they appeared before the Selecting Body on 19.05.2022. In
this writ petition, petitioners have sought the following relief:
"Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the selection Commission to
conclude to selection process initiated pursuant
to the advertisement dated 6th Nov 2020, by the
recommending name of the selected candidates
whose name figure in the Provisional Merit List
07th April 2022, as the document verification has
already been on conducted 19th May 2022."
In sum & substance, contention of the petitioners
is that since the result of written examination has been
declared on 07.04.2022 and, thereafter, document
verification has also been done, therefore, the delay in
appointing the selected candidates, is unwarranted.
On 13.07.2022, on the request of Mr. Pankaj
Purohit, learned counsel appearing for the Selecting
Body, the case was adjourned to enable him to get
instructions in the matter.
Today, on instructions, Mr. Pankaj Purohit,
Advocate submits that number of complaints were
received regarding irregularity in the selection process,
particularly the examination held on 04.12.2021 in
second shift and the Chairman of the Selecting Body
had issued a letter to Director General of Police; D.I.G.
(S.T.F.) and Principal Secretary, Home Department,
requesting them to conclude the on-going enquiry in
respect of the selection in question, within one month.
He further submits that, on 17.06.2022, similar request
was made to Additional Chief Secretary/ Home,
Government of Uttarakhand to get the on-going enquiry
concluded at the earliest. He further submits that as

10
soon as the report of the enquiry is received by the
Commission, and everything is found in order, the
names of selected candidates would be recommended to
the Competent Authority for further necessary action. It
is, thus, apparent that the selection process is not
concluded on account of on-going enquiry, therefore,
having regard to the facts & circumstances of the case,
the writ petition is disposed of with a direction to
respondent no. 4 to have the enquiry concluded as early
as possible, preferably within a period of ten weeks'
from the date of production of certified copy of the
order."
12. In the present case, the bone of contention is the segregation
of the candidates. Since the Special Task Force, who is holding the
investigation, has identified the tainted candidates, it is argued
that there is no occasion to withhold the appointment of the
selected untainted candidates.
13. The Commission filed its counter affidavit to the writ
petition, and contended that the question paper was heavily
circulated and leaked on the internet, which makes it highly
improbable for the Commission to segregate the students, who
are guilty, and who are innocent. Apart from this, the
Commission in paragraph 8 of the counter affidavit submits that
after investigation, Commission found that private firm "RMS
Techno Solution"-with whom the Commission entered into
contract to conduct multiple examinations, was also involved in
the irregularities and misconduct. The Special Task Force also
arrested the workers and some persons associated with this firm.
14. In paragraph 9 of the counter affidavit filed by the
Commission, it is contended that after due deliberation, the
Commission came to the conclusion that purely in the interest of
the candidates, who are aspirants for selection, a few

11
examinations- including present one, has to be cancelled in which
the said firm RMS Techno solution was involved, so that such
irregularity may not be happen in future, since the prime object
of the Commission is to maintain purity of the examination
process. The Commission submits that the decision for cancelling
the examination was taken after due deliberations with other
officials, and also in the light of judgments of the Supreme Court,
reference of which has been given in the office memorandum
dated 30.12.2022.
15. The learned Single Judge considered the following
submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioners,
which are as under:
"(i) It is not the case of paper leak or mass cheating.
(ii) The modus operandi of the wrong doers was that the
papers were given to chosen candidates, who were ready to
purchase it for consideration.
(iii) Those candidates were made to learn answers at some
isolated places, where they were not allowed to take any
devices, so as to avoid further leakage of question papers.
(iv) The investigation and the charge sheets establish that
the modus operandi was consideration for making question
papers available to the candidates at an isolated place.
(v) The STF in the month of February, 2023 could identify
only 114 persons and subsequently, the Commission by its
communication dated 12.04.2023, identified only 115
candidates, who were debarred from appearing in future
examinations to be conducted by the Commission.
(vi) Since the STF had identified the wrong doers and the
Commission had also identified the candidates, who used

12
unfair means in the examination, it is well established that
those who used unfair means were segregated. Therefore,
cancellation of the examination, as a whole, cannot be
sustained.
(vii) It is a case, in which segregation could have been done.
In fact, it has been argued that segregation has been done
by the STF and by the Commission also. (viii) The
petitioners are genuine candidates, who worked hard to
appear in the examination. They did not use unfair means.
They are selected candidates. Their hope would be shattered
if examination is cancelled. Their future prospects would be
adversely affected. Therefore, interest of such candidates
should also be protected in the larger interest.
(ix) The decision of the Commission for cancelling the
examination is unreasonable and arbitrary because the
decision is based on the report of the STF and the STF has
identified the wrong doers, beyond that the Commission
could not have travelled, by cancelling the examination.
(x) The STF was initially involved at the behest of the
Commission. In case, the STF was still investigating the
case, there was no hurry for the Commission to notify date
of reexamination. The Commission could have well waited
for the final conclusion drawn by the STF and thereafter,
could have taken a decision.
16. Shri A. S. Rawat, Sr. Advocate, who represented the
petitioners in WPSS No. 650 of 2023 raised following points in
respect of the reliefs, as sought in the writ petition:
"(i) Based on some screen shots some doubts were
created. It is the Commission which involved the STF
initially.

13
(ii) The modus operandi in the entire episode as per the STF
is restricted to a few identified persons. It is argued that
those wrong doers were identified by the STF.
(iii) As per the STF's investigation, such irregularities in
the examination were being done since 2015.
(iv) The STF identified 41 such agents, who were in search
of prospective candidates, those who could purchase the
question papers for consideration.
(v) One Abhishek Verma from RMS Techno Solution
would take screen shots of the question papers and
thereafter, it was released to other agents and finally the
question papers were made available to the aspiring
candidates for consideration.
(vi) The aspiring candidates were taken to isolated places to
memorise the question papers without the help of any
electronic device, so as to avoid any further leakage of the
question papers.
(vii) The wrong doers were distinctly identified by the STF.
The segregation was done. (viii) STF did file a charge sheet
with 58 persons and another charge sheet with 38 persons.
(ix) The petitioners are selected candidates. In case of
cancellation of their examination, the equality of
opportunity in public employment, as envisaged under
Article 16 of the Constitution of India would be frustrated.
17. So far as the Commission is concerned, it had also raised
certain points for submissions, which are as under:

14
"(i) The decision to cancel the examination is a conscious
decision taken by the Commission after evaluating every
possibility and keeping in view the larger public interest.
(ii) Not only complaints of the irregularities were noticed,
but the Commission has also found the OMR sheets, which
were viral on social media with the answers on it and the
order cancelling the examination records this fact.
(iii) The FIR in the matter has been lodged. There were
several candidates, whose names and addresses could not be
verified. Therefore, they could not be contacted.
(iv) It has also been surfaced during investigation by the
STF that some wrong doers did give question papers to
their wives and sisters in law. Thereafter, what happened to
those question papers, it is not known. It might have gone
to some other hands with further leakage of the question
papers.
(v) The Commission did debar 115 candidates from
appearing in future examinations. But, the investigation by
the STF is separate and is still continuing.
(vi) Nine charge sheets have already been filed and
investigation is still on."
18. So far as State/ respondents no. 1 to 3 are concerned, they
had not filed any counter affidavit, however, they had raised
following points:
"(i) The STF report reveals that the amount was paid for
question papers.
(ii) It is not possible to segregate the wrong doers from
those, who are genuine candidates.

15
(iii) The decision is based on the material that was before
the authority concerned.
(iv) The STF report cannot be ignored in such a serious
matter.
(v) The decision has been taken in the larger public interest
to maintain the purity of examination."
19. Learned Single Judge examined all the contentions raised
by learned counsel for the parties and discussed the entire issue
in the impugned judgment. Learned Single Judge-in paragraph
22 of the judgment, held that what is essentially challenged is a
policy decision - an administrative decision for cancellation of
examination. The scope of interference under Article 226 of the
Constitution of India in respect of such policy decision or
administrative decision has been dealt by learned Single Judge,
after relying upon the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case
of Tata Cellular Vs. Union of India (1994) 6 SCC 651. Apart from
aforesaid judgment, learned Single Judge also gave a reference of
judgments in relation to the scope of judicial review and
interference in respect of policy decision. Learned Single Judge
considered the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of
Gohil Vishvaraj Hanubhai and others Vs. State of Gujarat and
others, (2017) 13 SCC 621, wherein the extent of judicial review
permissible was also considered by the Supreme Court.
Paragraph 14 of the said judgment reads as under:
"14. Two questions need to be examined: 14.1. (i) What are
the principles which govern the jurisdiction of the courts
which exercise the power of judicial review of
administrative action in the context of a situation like the
one presented by the facts of these appeals?; 14.2. (ii)

16
Whether those legal principles are strictly followed by the
respondents while taking the impugned decision."
20. After dealing with several pronouncements of the Supreme
Court in respect of judicial review of administrative decision or
policy decision, the learned Single Judge in paragraph 26
examined the subject matter of the writ petition, by observing
that there may be genuine candidates who are not involved in
any irregularity, malpractice or unfair practice while
participating in the examination and, obviously, if examination is
cancelled, it will certainly cause irreparable loss and undue
harassment to such meritorious candidate-that too for no fault of
theirs. The learned Single Judge has observed that the decision of
the Commission for cancelling the examination is in larger public
interest. Learned Single Judge observed that if some candidates,
who were indulged in unfair means secured selection, then
certainly it will deny the appointment to other aspiring
candidates, who did not use any unfair means.
21. During the course of arguments, Mr. A.S. Rawat, learned Sr.
Advocate, also suggested before the learned Single Judge that
Special Task Force may be directed to conclude its investigation
and, based on such conclusion, the Commission may then be
required to take a decision to ascertain whether it is a case re-examination or segregation.
22. Argument of Mr. A.S. Rawat, Sr. Advocate was considered
by the learned Single Judge in the light of judgment of the
Supreme Court in the case of Gohil (supra), and he took into
consideration the observations made by the Supreme Court,
particularly in paragraph 30, which reads as under:
"30. Identifying all the candidates who are guilty of malpractice
either by criminal prosecution or even by an administrative

17
enquiry is certainly a time-consuming process. If it were to be the
requirement of law that such identification of the wrongdoers is a
must and only the identified wrongdoers be eliminated from the
selection process, and until such identification is completed the
process cannot be carried on, it would not only result in a great
inconvenience to the administration, but also result in a loss of
time even to the innocent candidates. On the other hand, by
virtue of the impugned action, the innocent candidates (for that
matter all the candidates including the wrongdoers) still get an
opportunity of participating in the fresh examination process to be
conducted by the State. The only legal disadvantage if at all is
that some of them might have crossed the upper age-limit for
appearing in the fresh recruitment process. That aspect of the
matter is taken care of by the State. Therefore, it cannot be said
that the impugned action is vitiated by lack of nexus with the
object sought to be achieved by the State, by herding all the
candidates at the examination together."
23. We have also examined the observations made by the
Supreme Court in paragraph 30 of the aforesaid judgment.
24. Learned Single Judge in the impugned judgment has also
examined the consequences of the cancellation of examination,
and: whether such decision is correct or not, has been examined
by the leaned Single Judge on the basis of rationality,
reasonableness, legality, proportionality, and procedural
propriety, which are some yardsticks.
25. Learned Single Judge has dealt with this aspect in the light
of judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Hanuman
Prasad and others Vs. Union of India and another (1996) 10 SCC
742. A reference has been made in paragraph 31 of the impugned
judgment. Learned Single Judge has further examined the

18
judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of B. Ramanjini and
others Vs. State of A.P. and others (2002) 5 SCC 533, wherein the
Supreme Court held that the courts ought not to take the action
lightly, and interfere with the same, particularly when there was
some material for the government to act one way or the other. In
paragraph 8 of the judgment, the Supreme Court observed as
follows:-
"8. Further, even if it was not a case of mass copying or
leakage of question papers or such other circumstance, it is
clear that in the conduct of the examination, a fair
procedure has to be adopted. Fair procedure would mean
that the candidates taking part in the examination must be
capable of competing with each other by fair means. One
cannot have an advantage either by copying or by having a
foreknowledge of the question paper or otherwise. In such
matters wide latitude should be shown to the Government
and the courts should not unduly interfere with the action
taken by the Government which is in possession of the
necessary information and takes action upon the same. The
courts ought not to take the action lightly and interfere
with the same particularly when there was some material
for the Government to act one way or the
other........................................................"
26. Learned Single Judge also examined the facts of the case
and has dealt the same in paragraph 33 of the judgment. We have
also examined the judgment, and we find that employees of the
"RMS Techno Solution"-with whom the Commission entered into
contract, were also involved and the two persons had taken
photographs on their mobile phone and forwarded it through
instagram. How these question papers were circulated, was also
highlighted by the learned Single Judge in paragraph 33 of the
judgment in a chronological manner. These two employees-Abhishek Verma and Jaiveer Das, had taken photograph of the
question paper from printing press in their mobile phones, and
then forwarded the same through instagram, and these question
papers were further forward to Manoj Joshi, Deepak Chauhan,

19
Bhawesh Jaguri and Deepak Chauwan. They memorized the
answer of these question papers and had memorised the same to
six candidates at the house of one of their relatives Geeta Ram
Panuli, and they collected Rs. 45 Lakh for the aspiring candidates.
The manner in which these questions were circulated in order to
collect money from the aspiring candidates goes to the root of the
matter.
27. The learned Single Judge, in paragraph 34 of the judgment,
gave reference of third charge-sheet, which reflects that the
owner of the RMS Techno Solution Mr. Rajesh Chauhan got the
answer papers memorised to the candidates in Vedanta Resorts
and Alpine Resorts in Danachuli Band, District Nainital. Some
answers were memorised at Raj Nagar extension at Ghaziabad,
some in other areas i.e. Haldwani, Bhimtal and Bijnor (Uttar
Pradesh). Learned Single Judge further made reference of 9
charge-sheets and details of persons against whom charge-sheet
were filed. Learned Single Judge also examined the office
memorandum issued by the Commission, whereby selection was
cancelled and re-examination of candidates, who participated in
the selection, was re-scheduled. Office memorandum records that
when the news of unfair means in the examination came to
surface, three handwritten OMR sheets were found circulating on
the social media. The office memorandum further records that
about 70-80 candidates could not be contacted, as their addresses
could not be verified. After examination of all the aspects and
material available on record, learned Single Judge examined -
whether cancellation of the examination by the Commission by
the impugned office memorandum dated 30.12.2022 is legal,
rational or proportional. Consequently, learned Single Judge,
after examining all the aspects of the matter in the light of several
judgments of the Supreme Court, came to the conclusion that the

20
cancellation of the examination cannot be termed as illegal,
irrational or unreasonable, since it was decision in the larger
public interest, so as to maintain the purity of the examination.
28. Mr. A. S. Rawat, Sr. Advocate for the petitioners -
appellants has questioned the judgment of learned Single Judge
on various grounds mentioned in the preceding paragraphs of
the judgment. This Court is not convinced with the argument
advanced by Mr. A.S. Rawat, Senior Advocate for the petitioners
- appellants, that it is a fit case for segregation of the candidates,
who have been found to be involved. Decision taken by the
impugned office memorandum by the Commission is not a
decision taken in haste, but the same has been taken after going
through the entire material available on record. The decision
taken by the Commission is well balanced in order to maintain
purity in public examination, which a logical and reasonable one.
We do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned
judgment passed by the learned Single Judge.
29. At this juncture, we, in fact, appreciate the conduct of the
Commission while taking a decision of cancelling the
examination and for conducting re-examination. What is
important is that in re-examination, only those candidates, who
appeared in the earlier examination, which was subsequently
cancelled, were allowed to participate. There was no decision for
re-advertisement of posts, therefore, petitioners - appellants
cannot say that they are seriously prejudiced. Even otherwise,
individual hardship cannot prevail over a policy decision, which
is meant for benefit of thousands of candidates, who have
legitimate expectation for their selection on their own merit.
What is relevant is that purity of the examination is maintained
and if Commission took such a decision for cancelling the

21
examination after collecting entire material, in the larger public
interest and to hold re-examination, we do not find any infirmity
in such decision of the Commission.
30. Even otherwise, an individual, who participated in the
selection does not get an enforceable right to be appointed till he
is selected and gets a letter of appointment. In the case in hand,
undisputedly, no appointment letters were issued to the
appellants. Therefore, order of cancellation of selection-which
emanated on the basis of complaints after holding an inquiry by
SIT, cannot be held to be unjustified. Since no legal rights accrued
in favour of the appellants, who participated in the selection, but
no appointment letters were issued, no mandamus can be issued
either for segregation or their appointment. Every selection
should be concluded in a transparent manner. Here, in the
present case, a large number of malpractices were found and
therefore, the Commission was perfectly justified in cancelling
the selection.
31. In view of the aforesaid observations, we do not find any
merit in the present appeal. Accordingly, the same is dismissed.
The impugned judgment rendered by the learned Single Judge is
hereby affirmed. No order as to costs.
